title: Windsor Logistics — post-demo technical action log
content:
Context:
- 2026-03-02 demo with Windsor Logistics (ops + infra + security). Goal: validate Redwood inference for ETA prediction and routing assistant in their driver ops console. They want a short pilot (6 weeks) to prove latency, throughput, and data controls before committing to Dedicated or Private.

Attendees:
- Windsor: Nina Patel (Head of Ops), Marco Alvarez (Platform), Soo Jin Park (Security), Tony Rhee (SRE)
- Redwood: Maya Chen (SE, owner), Liam O'Connor (solutions), Priya Nair (platform eng), Ethan Brooks (security eng)

High-level summary:
- Windsor liked the hosted API demo for speed of getting started but flagged two blockers: data residency/privacy for PII in driver notes, and predictable 99th percentile latency during peak dispatch windows (08:00–10:00 local).
- They asked about options: Redwood Hosted with tokenization + strict retention controls vs Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). They prefer Dedicated or Private for first pilot but want a minimal hosted path if Dedicated lead time is long.

Technical notes / requirements identified:
1) Workload profile (Marco):
   - Peak concurrency: ~420 concurrent inference requests in 10s bursts during morning peak.
   - Typical request size: 80–250 tokens input, expected response 40–120 tokens.
   - Embeddings for routing: batch of ~200 docs refreshed hourly.
2) Latency SLOs:
   - Target p50: <40ms token latency (end-to-end ~ <=300ms per request).
   - Target p99: <=800ms during peak. Critical to hit for UI snappiness.
3) Data constraints (Soo Jin):
   - Driver notes include PII (license plate, phone). Windsor must ensure data not stored beyond 7 days and be able to turn off retention quickly.
   - Audit logs required for all model calls and responses for 90 days (must be exportable).
4) Security stack:
   - KMS integration mandatory (customer-managed keys preferred).
   - VPN or VPC peering for Private deployment. Windsor prefers private control plane if possible.
5) Integration surface:
   - They will call Redwood API from their internal dispatch service in us-east-1.
   - Need SDK example in Go + Node for streaming responses (chat-like assistant in console).
6) Model behavior / quality:
   - Prefer a smaller deterministic model for ETA predictions, and a more capable assistant model for free-text suggestions. Will want A/B test of model variants.

Operational/gotchas observed in demo:
- Streaming assistant demo used a 4096 context; Windsor mostly uses 512–1024. Recommend setting default to 1024 to limit KV cache RAM on Dedicated nodes.
- Embedding refresh cadence: their hourly refresh of 200 docs is fine, but bulk recompute during index rebuilds could spike. Suggest staggered refresh and pre-warming caches.
- Token accounting: they were surprised by tokenization of driver metadata fields. Add guidance and sample pre-tokenization snippet to reduce cost.
- Fallback strategy: their UI cannot block on model timeouts. Must implement automatic fallback to cached quick responses or rule-based answer within 400ms to preserve UX.

Compliance / legal notes:
- Windsor wants a written matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — differences in data residency, retention, and auditability. Action: legal + security to produce a one-pager. (Owner: Ethan)

Preliminary capacity recommendation (SE suggestion):
- For pilot (6 weeks): 2 Dedicated inference workers configured as follows:
   * GPU type: A10 or equivalent for cost/throughput balance (good for batch embeddings + smaller model sampling)
   * Concurrency tuning: continuous batching with max_batch_size 64 and dynamic batching window 10ms during peak; adjust after one day of telemetry.
   * Cache: prefix cache enabled for repeated prompts (driver templates), KV cache limits set to avoid memory bloat (per-host kv-cap 10GB).
- If Windsor wants Private on-prem later, propose a 3-node cluster with autoscaling turned off for predictability, and a small bastion for control plane access.

PoC success criteria (agreed):
- Functional: assistant integrated in dispatch UI with streaming responses and fallback behavior.
- Perf: p99 <=800ms over 72-hour rolling window during peak traffic pattern.
- Cost: per-request inference spend <= projected budget (TBD) — need more Windsor cost targets.
- Security: KMS in place, retention configurable, audit logs export validated.

Immediate next steps (owners + target dates):
- Provide sample Go/Node streaming SDK snippets and pre-tokenization utils (Owner: Liam) — due 2026-03-05
- Deliver Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private comparison one-pager (Owner: Ethan + Priya) — due 2026-03-06
- Run short throughput test with Windsor synthetic workload (420 concurrent 10s bursts) against a Hosted test tenant to validate p99 (Owner: Priya) — schedule window 2026-03-08–2026-03-09
- Draft deployment checklist for Dedicated pilot (GPU sizing, kv cache, batching params, network) (Owner: Maya) — due 2026-03-07
- Confirm KMS requirements and onboarding steps (Owner: Soo Jin at Windsor + Ethan) — sync by 2026-03-04

Open questions to resolve:
- Windsor licensing constraints: do they require an air-gapped on-prem option or is VPC Private acceptable? (Windsor security to confirm.)
- Cost threshold for pilot: need Windsor finance to provide target monthly inference spend to decide between A10 vs A100.
- Embedding store: do they want Redwood-managed vector DB or will they manage their own (they currently run a self-hosted Redis+FAISS)?

Quick notes to remember for follow-up demo:
- Show model variant A/B dashboard in Console and how to rollback to lower-capacity variant automatically.
- Demo audit log export (CSV + S3) and retention toggle UI in Console.
- Include an example of the fallback policy config (rule-based + cached response) in rollout docs.

End of notes.
